title: Vector proofs
examples: How do I know if three points are on the same line?
What does it mean for two vectors to be parallel?
Can you show me an example using coordinates?

explain.say: Today we learn to prove things using vectors. We will look at three main ideas. These ideas are collinearity, parallel vectors, and ratios.
First we look at collinearity. Three points A, B, and C are collinear if they all lie on the same straight line. We can check this using vectors.

items: Points A, B, C are collinear

explain.say: If the vector AB is a multiple of the vector AC, then the points are collinear. This means one vector is a scalar multiple of the other vector. For example, if $\vec{AB} = 2\vec{AC}$, the points A, B, and C are on a line.

items: Points A, B, C are collinear

explain.say: Next we look at parallel vectors. Two vectors are parallel if one is a scalar multiple of the other. This is the same condition as collinearity, but we focus on the direction.

items: One vector is a scalar multiple

draw.text: Parallel: One vector is a scalar multiple

explain.say: For example, if $\vec{PQ} = -3\vec{RS}$, then the vectors PQ and RS are parallel. The negative sign just means they point in opposite directions.

items: Vectors PQ and RS are parallel

faq.a: Three points are collinear if the vector connecting the first two points is a scalar multiple of the vector connecting any two other points. You can also check if the area of the triangle formed by them is zero.
asks: How do I prove points are on a line?
What does it mean for points to be collinear?

faq.q: What is the difference between parallel and collinear?
faq.a: Collinear means the points themselves are on the same line. Parallel vectors mean the vectors point in the same or opposite direction, but the points might not be connected in a line.
asks: Does parallel mean the points are in a line?

faq.q: What does the scalar multiple $k$ tell me?
faq.a: The scalar $k$ tells you the ratio between the vectors. If $k$ is positive, they point the same way. If $k$ is negative, they point opposite ways.
asks: What does the number in front mean?
How does the ratio affect the direction?

faq.q: Can I use coordinates to check for collinearity?
faq.a: Yes, you can calculate the vectors using the coordinates. Then you check the ratio between the components of the resulting vectors.
asks: Do I need coordinates for this?
How do I use coordinates here?

faq.a: If the scalar is zero, it means the vector $\vec{AB}$ must be the zero vector, so points A and B must be the same point.
asks: What if the scalar is zero?
If the vector equals zero, what is true?

facts: If $\vec{AB} = k\vec{AC}$, then points A, B, and C are collinear.
If $\vec{PQ} = k\vec{RS}$, then the vectors are parallel.
The scalar $k$ represents the ratio between the corresponding components of the vectors.
If $k=1$, the vectors are equal and point the same way.

quiz.say: If $\vec{XY} = 3\vec{XZ}$, are points X, Y, and Z collinear?
quiz.why: Because the vector $\vec{XY}$ is a scalar multiple of $\vec{XZ}$, the points must lie on the same line.

wrong.1: This is tempting because you might think a multiple means they are separate.
wrong.2: This is wrong because a negative scalar still keeps them on the same line.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the relationship holds even if the vector $\vec{XZ}$ is not zero.

quiz.say: Which condition proves that vectors $\vec{PQ}$ and $\vec{RS}$ are parallel?
quiz.why: Two vectors are parallel if one can be written as a scalar multiple of the other vector.

wrong.0: This condition proves the vectors are perpendicular, not parallel.
wrong.1: This only proves they are equal, which is a special case of being parallel.
wrong.3: This only proves they are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, not just parallel.

quiz.say: If $\vec{AB} = \langle 2, 4 \rangle$ and $\vec{AC} = \langle 1, 2 \rangle$, what is the relationship between the vectors?
quiz.why: You check if the components of $\vec{AB}$ are exactly two times the components of $\vec{AC}$.

wrong.0: This would mean the vectors are perpendicular, which is not the case here.
wrong.1: This cross product method is usually for 3D space, not the simplest check here.
wrong.3: This would only be true if the scalar multiple was exactly one.
